title: What If You Stopped Blinking?

scenes.text: What if you stopped blinking? Your eyes would start to suffer.
Normally you blink about fifteen times a minute, more than fourteen thousand times a day.
Each blink spreads a film of tears across your eye, keeping the surface smooth and moist.
Without it, the film dries out. Vision blurs, and the dryness can feel like a scratch on your cornea.
Your cornea has no blood vessels, so blinks also bring it oxygen. Without them, it can swell.
A blink lasts a fraction of a second, yet you spend about ten percent of your waking time with your eyes closed.

description:
What if you stopped blinking?
Blinks spread tears, bring oxygen to the cornea and clear debris, so blinking less can cause dryness, blurry vision and swelling.
